title: Where a question has no answer, the frontend's review page prints 'Not provided' and DR1 prints 'Not applicable'.

finding.frontend: An empty answer renders as the string 'Not provided', held once in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/copy/copy.en.js:3 and used by every row builder under check-answers/view-model/rows/. The captured page shows it against Region of origin code, Internal reference number and Number of packages.
finding.prototype: An empty answer renders as 'Not applicable' — every review row value passes through formatReviewValueOrNa, which substitutes that phrase for a null or blank value (app/routes.js:4065-4071). The captured page shows it against Region of origin code and Internal reference number.
finding.difference: Change the placeholder on Check your answers from 'Not provided' to 'Not applicable' in the English and Welsh copy files for the check-answers feature. It is one string in each. Note that DR1 only uses this phrase on a card it considers complete — on an incomplete card it blanks the value instead, which is the separate finding about reporting incompleteness on the review page.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a DR1 review row that prints 'Not provided' for an unanswered question.
finding.correction: Stands, and both halves are visible in the pictures. The frontend's captured review page prints 'Not provided' against Region of origin code, Internal reference number and Number of packages; DR1's prints 'Not applicable' against Region of origin code and Internal reference number. The string 'Not provided' does not occur anywhere in dr1-review-notification.html and 'Not applicable' does not occur anywhere in fe-check-answers.html. Both citations are exact — copy.en.js:3 is `notProvided: 'Not provided'` and app/routes.js:4065-4071 is formatReviewValueOrNa. The caveat in `difference` about DR1 blanking rather than substituting on an incomplete card is also right and worth keeping: isReviewValueEmpty (app/routes.js:4073-4077) counts the literal string 'Not applicable' as empty, which is how a row already carrying the placeholder gets blanked when its card is in error. CONTROLS FIXED, AND THE FINDING IS UNCHANGED BY IT. This finding named the two placeholder strings themselves, 'Not provided' and 'Not applicable'. Each is present on one side and absent from the other, which is the finding, but each is also repeated furniture — 'Not provided' sits on three rows of fe-check-answers and 'Not applicable' on two rows of dr1-review-notification — so on the side where it exists the resolver refused to guess which row was meant, and on the side where it does not exist there was nothing to find. Neither side got a crop, and the finding was left with no element evidence for a difference that is visible in one glance. The control a user actually meets is the review row, so the finding now names 'Region of origin code', which occurs once on each side's review page and is the row both slots already cite. The pair of crops it produces is the finding in two pictures: 'Region of origin code — Not provided' on the frontend against 'Region of origin code — Not applicable' on DR1. The placeholder strings stay named in the prose, where they belong; they were never things anyone could point at.

relatedTo.why: DR1 replaces this placeholder with a blank on a card it has flagged incomplete
